llm.summary: The skill is a simple scaffolding helper that creates a workspace and registers a new agent; it does not request credentials or download external code, but it does not automatically configure channel credentials/bindings — those edits are manual.

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim to 'create a new agent and connect it to a messaging channel.' The included script and SKILL.md create a workspace and register the agent with the OpenClaw CLI (agents.add). They do NOT automatically populate channel account entries or the top-level bindings in openclaw.json — the SKILL.md instructs the user to add those manually. This is a small capability mismatch (advertised 'connect' vs. manual configuration), but otherwise the requested operations align with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and the script are limited to creating files under ~/.openclaw (or OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR), backing up openclaw.json, and calling the openclaw CLI to add the agent. The SKILL.md instructs the user to edit openclaw.json and run openclaw gateway restart/pairing. The script reads an optional OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR env var and writes/backs up openclaw.json — expected for registration, but worth noting because it modifies configuration files in the user's OpenClaw state.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; this is an instruction-only skill with a small bundled shell script. The script is local, does not fetch remote archives or execute downloaded code, and writes only to the user's OpenClaw state directory. Low install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The script optionally respects OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR to change the state path, which is reasonable for a tool that manipulates gateway state. Channel credentials (tokens, app secrets, QR logins) are required by the platform and are intentionally never requested by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated or persistent platform privileges. It writes its own workspace files and backs up openclaw.json, but does not modify other skills or inject into unrelated system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is primarily a scaffold and registration helper — it will create a workspace under your OpenClaw state directory and attempt a non-interactive agent registration via the openclaw CLI, and it will back up openclaw.json. Before running: (1) Verify the script contents (they are included) and confirm you have the openclaw CLI installed. (2) Note that channel account entries and top-level bindings must be added to openclaw.json manually (the skill does not auto-add tokens/bindings). (3) Keep bot tokens, app secrets, and service-account JSON out of chat prompts and paste them only into your config file or the platform's secure place. (4) The skill source/homepage are not provided here — if provenance matters, verify the repository referenced in the README (or obtain the skill from a trusted source) before use. If unsure, run the script in a test environment and inspect the created backup of openclaw.json.
